desc:
You are given an integer array nums and a list of queries. Each query is a pair [l, r] (0-indexed, both ends inclusive) asking: how many different values occur in the subarray nums[l..r]?

Return an array with the answer to each query, in the original order.

For example, nums = [1, 2, 1, 3, 2] and queries = [[0, 4], [0, 2], [2, 3], [1, 1]] give [3, 2, 2, 1].

With thousands of queries, building a set for each subarray is too slow in the worst case (O(n) per query); look for something close to O((n + q) log n).
hints: A value counts for the query [l, r] once, no matter how many copies lie inside. Choose one 'representative' occurrence per value.
Process the queries offline, sorted by right end r, while sweeping a pointer over the array. For a fixed sweep position, make the last occurrence of every value its representative.

Keep a Fenwick tree (binary indexed tree) over positions with a 1 at each representative. When you reach position p with value x, remove the 1 at the previous occurrence of x (if any) and add a 1 at p. The answer to a query is the sum over positions l..r.
editorial: Sort queries by right endpoint and sweep the array from left to right. After processing position r, mark exactly one position per value: its most recent occurrence at or before r. For a query [l, r], a value occurs in the range exactly when its latest occurrence up to r is at index ≥ l, so the number of marked positions in [l, r] equals the number of distinct values.

Marks change in O(1) positions per step: when moving to index p with value x, unmark the previous occurrence of x and mark p. A Fenwick tree supports these point updates and the prefix sums for range counting in O(log n). Total time is O((n + q) log n) plus sorting the queries, with O(n + q) space. The brute-force alternative of building a set for each query takes O(n) per query, up to O(nq) overall.
solution:
def distinctInRanges(nums, queries):
    n = len(nums)
    tree = [0] * (n + 1)

    def update(i, d):
        i += 1
        while i <= n:
            tree[i] += d
            i += i & -i

    def prefix(i):
        # sum of positions 0..i (0 when i < 0)
        i += 1
        s = 0
        while i > 0:
            s += tree[i]
            i -= i & -i
        return s

    order = sorted(range(len(queries)), key=lambda q: queries[q][1])
    last = {}
    res = [0] * len(queries)
    p = 0
    for q in order:
        l, r = queries[q]
        while p <= r:
            x = nums[p]
            if x in last:
                update(last[x], -1)
            update(p, 1)
            last[x] = p
            p += 1
        res[q] = prefix(r) - prefix(l - 1)
    return res
